newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch BNG wants funding in euros from 1999.
newsitem.headline: Dutch BNG wants funding in euros from 1999.

text.p: Dutch local authorities bank NV Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten (BNG) said on Thursday it was making preparations for the introduction of the euro, the single European currency, in January 1999.
"From that date, a substantial part of the BNG funding will be taken up in euros," BNG said in a statement.

The bank, which finances Dutch public authorities, is the second largest issuer of debt in the Netherlands after the Dutch state. In 1996, it borrowed about 12 billion guilders in Dutch and foreign capital markets, compared with about nine billion in the previous year.
For the first time, BNG entered the Japanese capital market in 1996 and it issued two loans in France.
"The bank's triple-A rating was an important factor for this," BNG said.

It added that its balance sheet total had grown by almost six percent to 109 billion guilders in 1996 and that its profits had grown by about five percent. In 1995, the unlisted BNG posted a net profit of 300 million guilders.
